claims.claim: For d=δ⁺(D)≥1, a directed cycle of length at least d+1 can be found in polynomial time; additionally, n<d+k is an immediate sound NO condition. Thus the target is completely solved for k=1.
claims.evidence: For a maximal simple directed path P=v₁…v_p, every out-neighbor of v_p lies among v₁,…,v_{p−1}. If v_i is the earliest such neighbor, the at least d distinct out-neighbors occupy positions i through p−1, so p−i≥d. Closing at v_i gives a directed cycle with p−i+1≥d+1 vertices. Greedy extension and extraction are polynomial. Since every cycle has at most n vertices, n<d+k is a sound NO condition; for k=1 the constructive lower bound always reaches the target.
claims.search_method: Reconstructed the maximal-path proof and exhaustively checked all 4,164 loopless digraphs on 2–4 vertices, including the stated greedy construction, using exact Boolean bitsets.

claims.claim: For any integer L≥2, existence of a directed cycle of length at least L is exactly equivalent to a short-leg two-way linkage, yielding an explicit O(n^L(n+m)) exact algorithm.
claims.evidence: Given an enumerated simple L-vertex path v₁…v_L, a simple v_L-to-v₁ path after deleting v₂,…,v_{L−1} intersects the first path only at its endpoints, so their union is a simple directed cycle of length at least L. Conversely, L consecutive vertices of any qualifying cycle form the enumerated path, and the remaining cycle segment is the required return path. There are at most n^L tuples and each reachability test costs O(n+m); tuple validation is absorbed because L≤n after immediately rejecting L>n.
claims.search_method: Checked both implications directly and compared the linkage predicate with exact subset-DP circumference over 16,584 graph/threshold pairs from every loopless digraph on 2–4 vertices.

claims.claim: There is a polynomially checkable upper-bound certificate: if X is an independent vertex set and every arc entering X from outside X has its tail in S⊆V(D)\X, then every directed cycle has length at most n−|X|+|S|.
claims.evidence: For each x∈C∩X, independence puts its predecessor on C outside X, and the entering-arc hypothesis puts that predecessor in C∩S. Different x have different predecessors because each cycle vertex has only one successor on C. Hence |C∩X|≤|C∩S|≤|S|, while |C\X|≤n−|X|, yielding |C|≤n−|X|+|S|. All certificate conditions and the inequality are directly polynomially checkable.
claims.search_method: Reconstructed the injective predecessor argument and exhaustively tested 131,755 valid (digraph,X,S) certificates on all loopless digraphs through four vertices against exact circumference.

claims.claim: For every fixed k≥4 there are 2-strong NO-instances with arbitrarily large minimum outdegree and with n≥d+k; indeed their circumference is exactly d+3.
claims.evidence: In the stated construction, deleting any vertex leaves at least one of x,y, through which every surviving core vertex can reach A; vertices of A reach the surviving complete bidirected core directly. Thus every deletion is strong. Outdegrees are q−1 for Q\{x,y}, q for A, and q−1+a for x,y, so d=q−1. Only x and y send arcs into A, so a simple cycle contains at most two A-vertices and has length at most q+2. The exhibited cycle through all q core vertices and two A-vertices has length q+2=d+3. Choosing a≥k−1 gives n=q+a≥q−1+k=d+k, while d+3<d+k for k≥4; taking q arbitrarily large makes d arbitrarily large.
claims.search_method: Verified the construction algebraically and used exact reachability and subset dynamic programming on all 30 parameter pairs 3≤q≤7 and 2≤a≤7, checking every vertex deletion, minimum outdegree, circumference, and applicable k.

claims.claim: The target has a polynomial-time solution on semicomplete digraphs: such an input is YES exactly when n≥d+k, and a Hamiltonian directed cycle can be constructed when YES.
claims.evidence: The target's inputs are 2-strong and hence strong. For a nonspanning directed cycle C in a strong semicomplete digraph, either an outside vertex inserts between consecutive vertices of C, or every outside vertex is uniformly dominated by C or uniformly dominates C. The latter classification follows by propagating the absence of an insertion around C. Strongness forces both classes and a directed arc from the first class to the second along a path toward C; those two vertices can be inserted together. Repetition constructs a Hamiltonian cycle in polynomial time. Consequently a target cycle exists exactly when its requested length d+k does not exceed n.
claims.search_method: Completed the constructive insertion proof and exhaustively checked all 59,808 semicomplete digraphs on 2–5 vertices. Every one of the 52,528 strong instances was Hamiltonian; the 19,777 2-strong instances also satisfied the stated threshold equivalence for all tested k.

target_evidence: The exact target asks for an f(k)n^{O(1)} algorithm on all 2-strong digraphs that constructs a cycle of length at least δ⁺(D)+k or correctly reports NO. The draft does not provide that algorithm: its general exact algorithm has exponent L=d+k, while its polynomial algorithms cover only k=1 and the semicomplete subclass. The upper-bound certificate and explicit NO-family are correct structural progress but do not close the general algorithmic target. The final writeup expressly states that the required FPT algorithm was not obtained and labels the resolution partial, so claimed_resolution is ACCURATE and the headline does not overclaim coverage.
checks_performed: Read only the authorized source input and baseline draft; independently compared the exact FPT target with the draft's achieved scope.
